command_words_note: OCR J625: Category 1 (AO1 recall) = Name/State/Give (low tariff). Category 2 (AO1 K&U) = Describe/Outline (3 & 6 mark). Category 3 (AO2 analysis/eval) = Explain/Compare (6 mark). Category 4 (AO1+AO2 extended) = '<statement>. Discuss.' (15 mark). Group 1 papers = two 5-part questions (AO1 60/AO2 40). Group 2 themes = four 4-part questions (AO1 40/AO2 60). SPaG assessed on extended responses.
structure_note: Cover-all 14-unit build so any OCR centre is served. Component Group 1: each religion split into a Beliefs & Teachings unit and a Practices unit (5 religions; OCR has NO Sikhism). Component Group 2: the four themes are studied through ONE chosen religion but assessed identically across religions, so we ship them as standalone multi-faith units drawing primarily on the Christianity treatment (J625/06) with the Islam treatment (J625/07) as a second-religion lens. OCR spec is source-of-wisdom rich; section_markers list ONLY citations that actually appear in the spec. Transfer from existing free-tier religious-studies-aqa / religious-studies-edexcel siblings where the doctrine matches, but OCR's named scripture anchors and command-word framing differ, so regenerate practice questions fresh.

article_units.name: Christianity: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: The nature of God, the Trinity, creation, evil, Jesus, salvation and the last things

lessons.title: The Nature of God and the Trinity
lessons.description: God as benevolent, omnipotent, just and eternal; the Trinity of three persons; common and divergent emphases.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the terms: benevolent, omniscient, omnipotent, monotheistic, judge, eternal, transcendent, immanent, personal, forgiving
The significance for Christians of these characteristics
The common and divergent emphases placed on these characteristics by different Christian denominations
The concept of the Trinity as one God, three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit)
The relationship between Father, Son and Holy Spirit
Issues related to the Nature of God; different attitudes to God as a Trinity
Different interpretations and emphases given to sources of wisdom and authority by different Christian denominations
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Beliefs L1 (Trinity & nature of God) — regenerate with OCR anchors (Matthew 6:9-15, Philippians 2:5-8, Apostles'/Nicene Creed)

lessons.title: Creation and the Problem of Evil
lessons.description: God as creator in Genesis and John 1; the Fall and original sin; natural and moral evil and the problem of suffering.
spec_coverage: The concept of God as creator; the role of God the Father as creator in the Genesis narrative
The role of the Spirit in Genesis 1-2 as the agent of God; the role of the Word in John 1
The identification of Jesus in John's Gospel chapter 1 as the Word of God linking him to creation and his pre-existence
The role and purpose of human beings; the Fall in the Genesis narrative
Issues raised in Genesis for different Christian groups: literal interpretations and metaphorical understandings
Concepts of evil; different types of evil: natural evil and moral evil; causes of evil
The Fall of mankind as the result of Free Will; the concept of original sin; the concept of Good
The problem of the existence of evil and suffering: how an omnipotent God can allow evil and suffering if he is also benevolent and righteous
section_markers: the problem of evil and suffering
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Beliefs (creation) + problem-of-evil material from Theme; OCR groups creation with evil — anchor Genesis 1-3, John 1, Book of Job

lessons.title: Jesus Christ: Incarnation, the Cross and Salvation
lessons.description: Jesus as Messiah and Saviour; agape; incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection, ascension; salvation and atonement.
spec_coverage: The meaning and significance of the terms Messiah, Son of God, Lord and Saviour as descriptions of Jesus, and their relevance for Christians today
The role and importance of Jesus' teachings and life as an example for Christians; Christian love (agape); the Christian ideal in the Sermon on the Mount
The meaning of the terms the incarnation, the crucifixion, the resurrection and the ascension, and beliefs and teachings about Jesus arising from them
The importance to Christians of the incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection and ascension for their life and worship; common and divergent denominational emphases
The meaning of the terms Salvation, Atonement, Law, Sin, Grace and Spirit
The role of Christ in salvation: the sacrifice of Christ paying the ransom to God for the sins of the world
Issues related to salvation: forgiveness and repentance for all; the nature of atonement; common and divergent Christian beliefs about the need for salvation and the role of Jesus Christ
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Beliefs (incarnation + salvation/atonement) — merge; OCR anchors Romans 3:23/6:23/3:24, Ephesians 2:8-9, Sermon on the Mount

lessons.title: Eschatological Beliefs: Death, Judgement and the Afterlife
lessons.description: Resurrection, life after death and the Parousia; beliefs about death, judgement, purgatory, heaven and hell.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the terms resurrection, life after death, heaven and hell
Apocalyptic ideas in the Early Church
Common and divergent beliefs about the Second Coming of Christ (Parousia)
Common and divergent beliefs about, and interpretations of, death, judgement, purgatory, heaven and hell
Different interpretations and emphases given to sources of wisdom and authority by different Christian denominations
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Beliefs (afterlife) — OCR adds Parousia and apocalyptic framing; anchor 1 Corinthians 15:12-58, John 14:1-3, Matthew 25:31-46

article_units.name: Christianity: Practices
article_units.subtitle: Worship, sacraments, prayer, pilgrimage, festivals, mission and the worldwide Church

lessons.title: Worship, Sacraments and Prayer
lessons.description: Liturgical and informal worship; the meaning of sacraments, baptism and Eucharist; the types and use of prayer.
spec_coverage: The structure of church services, e.g. Anglican Communion service, Roman Catholic mass, Quaker meeting, Greek Orthodox service and Methodist Sunday morning worship
The concept and purposes of worship; the role and importance of liturgical worship and of informal/charismatic worship for some Christians
The role and importance of individual, private and public prayer and worship to Christian communities and individuals
The meaning of the word sacrament; the role and meaning of the sacraments; the role of Baptism and Eucharist in the life of a Christian
Common and divergent attitudes towards the practice and meaning of Baptism and the Eucharist, and towards which practices are considered a sacrament by different denominations
The concept, impact and importance of prayer; the importance of prayer in worship; the meaning and use of the Lord's Prayer in individual and communal worship

The different types and uses of prayer including adoration, confession, thanksgiving, supplications, grace, intercessions, 'praying in the spirit', chants and meditational prayers; informal extempore vs set liturgical prayer
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Practices (worship + sacraments + prayer) — merge; OCR anchors 1 Corinthians 11:23-26, Matthew 26:26-28, Luke 11:1-4

lessons.title: Pilgrimage, Festivals and the Local Church Community
lessons.description: Pilgrimage to Lourdes, Jerusalem, Walsingham and Rome; Christmas and Easter; rites of passage and church life.
spec_coverage: The concept of pilgrimage; the purpose of pilgrimage to Lourdes, Jerusalem, Walsingham and Rome; the impact of pilgrimage on individuals and communities
The origin of Christmas and Easter; the impact and importance of Advent and Christmas, and of Lent, Holy Week and Easter celebrations to Christians
Common and divergent attitudes towards the importance of pilgrimages and celebrations by different Christian denominations
The meaning and importance of rites of passage; the importance of Christian rituals that mark key rites of passage to individuals and communities
The ways in which church communities nurture and support families, e.g. Sunday schools, youth clubs, mother and child groups, visiting the elderly and the sick
Common and divergent attitudes and practices connected with membership (infant baptism, dedication, believers' baptism, confirmation), marriage and funerals
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Practices (pilgrimage + festivals) — OCR-named sites Lourdes/Jerusalem/Walsingham/Rome; add rites of passage + church-in-community

lessons.title: Mission, Evangelism, Ecumenism and the Persecuted Church
lessons.description: Mission and evangelism; new forms of church; the World Council of Churches, Taize, Iona and a Christian aid agency.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the term mission and its importance in the modern church; common and divergent attitudes towards mission for Christians in 21st century Britain
The meaning of the term evangelism; evangelism in practice; the growth of new forms of church and reasons for it
The meaning of the term Ecumenical; the meaning of the word Church (spiritual and temporal) and of churches as individual communities
The main purpose of the World Council of Churches, including reconciliation through ecumenism; the work of ecumenical communities, e.g. Taize, Iona, Corrymeela and the 'Churches Together' movement
The way in which the Church is being persecuted in the 21st century and supporting the persecuted church
The purpose of one of the following Christian aid agencies: Christian Aid, Tearfund, Cafod
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Christianity Practices (mission + worldwide church) — OCR-named ecumenical communities Taize/Iona/Corrymeela; pick ONE aid agency

article_units.name: Islam: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: Core beliefs, the nature of Allah, prophethood, holy books, angels and life after death

lessons.title: Core Beliefs: Six Articles and the Five Roots
lessons.description: The Six Articles of Sunni Islam, the Five Roots of Shi'a Islam, and the belief about justice and imamate.
spec_coverage: The six articles of faith in Sunni Islam: belief in Allah, angels, holy books, the Prophets, the Day of Judgement and Predestination; the overall importance of the six articles for Sunni Muslims
The meaning of 'Usul ad-Din' (The Principles of Faith)
The five roots of 'Usul ad-Din' in Shi'a Islam: Al-Tawhid, Al-Adl, Al-Nubuwwah, Al-Imamah, Al-Ma'ad; the overall importance of the five roots for Shi'ite Muslims
Issues related to core beliefs in Sunni and Shi'a Islam; belief about justice and imamate (leadership) which differentiates Shi'a Islam from Sunni Islam
Common and divergent attitudes of different groups of Muslims towards core beliefs
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Beliefs (Six Articles + Five Roots) — OCR explicitly contrasts Sunni six articles vs Shi'a five roots; anchor Surah 4:136, Hadith al-Thaqalayn

lessons.title: The Nature of Allah
lessons.description: The 99 names of Allah; Tawhid and shirk; implications for polytheism and Christianity; the Shi'a Imamate.
spec_coverage: The importance for Muslims of the 99 names of Allah with specific knowledge of Tawhid (oneness), Merciful, Omnipotent, Benevolent, Fair and Just, Transcendent, Immanent
The meaning of Tawhid and its relationship to the concept of shirk
The implications of Tawhid and shirk for polytheism and Christianity
Issues related to the Nature of Allah and how these attributes are shown: Allah's role as creator and judge (omnipotence), His intervention (immanence), His guidance (merciful nature)
The Shi'a concept of the Imamate and its relationship to Shi'a belief in Tawhid
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Beliefs (Tawhid & nature of Allah) — OCR anchors Surah 112, Surah 50:16; stress shirk vs polytheism/Christianity

lessons.title: Prophethood, Holy Books and Angels
lessons.description: The prophets from Adam to Muhammad; the revealed books; the Qur'an; the angels Jibril, Izra'il, Mika'il and Israfil.
spec_coverage: The role and importance of the prophets: Adam (created from clay, khalifa), Ibrahim (father of the prophets, a hanif), Isma'il (and the Kaaba), Musa (the 10 commandments), Dawud (the Zabur, victory over Goliath), Isa (not divine but a messenger)

Muhammad (PBUH) as 'seal of the prophets' and the implications of this; Risalah as Allah's way of communicating with humans; the belief in the twelve Imams and their infallible nature (imamate) in Shi'a Islam
Islam as the original religion dating back to Adam; the Scrolls (Sahifah), Gospel (Injil), Torah (Tawrat) and Psalms (Zabur) revealed to four previous messengers
The original belief system was the same for all but became distorted; the Qur'an as the final undistorted message
The role and importance of Jibril (chief angel), Izra'il (taking the final breath), Mika'il (guardian of heaven, bringer of thunder) and Israfil (the trumpet on the Day of Judgement)
Angels as Allah's first creation: immortal, free of sin and without free will; recording angels and how belief in them may affect behaviour
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Beliefs (Risalah + Holy Books + Angels) — OCR names Israfil as 4th angel and the twelve Imams; anchor Surah 96, Surah 5:46

lessons.title: Predestination and Life After Death (Akhirah)
lessons.description: Al-Qadr as divine masterplan and human free will; Akhirah, Barzakh, judgement, al-Jannah and Jahannam.
spec_coverage: Predestination (al-Qadr) as a divine masterplan; the idea of sifat (Allah's foreknowledge) and free will for humans; human freedom and its relationship to the Day of Judgement
Knowledge of faith and action recorded in each individual's book of life and read out on the Day of Judgement; common and divergent attitudes towards human freedom: Mu'tazilite and Al-Ashari
The meaning of the term Akhirah; life as preparation for the life to come after the Day of Judgement; human responsibility and accountability; the Islamic concept of stewardship
Barzakh as the period between death and the Day of Judgement; descriptions of heaven (al-Jannah) and hell (Jahannam)
Literal and metaphorical interpretations of heaven and hell; the issue of martyrdom
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Beliefs (al-Qadr + Akhirah) — OCR adds Barzakh, Mu'tazilite/Al-Ashari debate; anchor Surah 17:49-51, Surah 101

article_units.name: Islam: Practices
article_units.subtitle: The Five Pillars, the Ten Obligatory Acts, worship, Hajj, festivals and Jihad

lessons.title: The Five Pillars, the Ten Obligatory Acts and Worship
lessons.description: The Five Pillars, the Ten Obligatory Acts and Shahadah; public and private worship; Salah, wudu and du'a.
spec_coverage: Islam as a way of life lived in total submission to Allah; the importance and meaning of the Five Pillars to Sunni Muslims: Shahadah, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj; the analogy of the house and pillars
The importance and meaning of the Ten Obligatory Acts to Shi'a Muslims: Salat, Sawm, Zakat, Khums, Hajj, Jihad, Amr-bil-Maroof, Nahi Anil Munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra
How and why Muslims pray: ablution (wudu), times, directions, movements and recitations in the home, mosque and elsewhere; the purpose of congregational prayers and the khutba

The place of Shahadah in Muslim practice (first words to a newborn, conversion, said by/to the dying); Shahadah as the only 'non-action' pillar; the declaration la ilaha illa-llah, muhammadur-rasulu-llah
Salah as direct communication with Allah; who has to attend Jummah prayers; the meaning of niyyah, qibla and raka't
The meaning of the term du'a (personal prayer or supplication); the importance of private acts of worship; the difference between du'a prayers and salah
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Practices (Five Pillars + Salah) — OCR lists the full Ten Obligatory Acts and du'a vs salah; anchor Surah 4:103, Surah 2:186

lessons.title: Hajj, Zakah, Khums and Sawm
lessons.description: Hajj and its rituals; the role of Zakah and Khums and the idea of Nisab; fasting in Ramadan and the Night of Power.
spec_coverage: The importance of pilgrimage for Muslims; Hajj as the obligatory pilgrimage; its origins; how and why it is performed; the exceptions to Hajj; Ihram regulations; the rituals of Hajj and their significance
The meaning of Zakah and Khums; the role and importance of giving alms: origins, how/why alms should be given, the benefits; Khums as an additional form of giving (Shi'a)
The Muslim attitude towards wealth as given by Allah; Sadaqah as voluntary alms; the idea of Nisab (2.5%); the distribution of alms; how Khums and Zakah are separate and apportioned
The role and importance of fasting in Ramadan: the origins of fasting, fasting as devotion to Allah, duties, benefits, exemptions, the Night of Power
Ramadan as the month the Qur'an was sent down to mankind; different experiences for Muslims in Muslim and non-Muslim countries
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Practices (Zakah + Hajj + Sawm) — OCR adds Khums/Nisab detail and Night of Power; anchor Surah 22:26-38, Surah 9:60

lessons.title: Festivals and Jihad
lessons.description: Eid-ul-Adha, Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Ghadeer and Ashura; greater and lesser Jihad and the conditions for Lesser Jihad.
spec_coverage: The origin and meaning of Eid-ul-Adha (the festival of sacrifice at the end of Hajj, Ibrahim's sacrifice) and Eid-ul-Fitr (the end of Ramadan)
The origin and meaning of Eid-ul-Ghadeer (a Shi'a festival celebrating the appointment of Ali) and Ashura (commemorating the martyrdom of Hussayn in 680CE)
The importance of these festivals for different groups of Muslims; issues for Muslims living in Muslim and non-Muslim countries
The meaning and importance of Greater Jihad (the struggle to live according to 'the straight path') and Lesser Jihad (removing evil from society); the precedence of Greater over Lesser Jihad
Conditions for the declaration and conduct of Lesser Jihad; the concepts of Munkar and Ma'ruf; common and divergent views about if and when the holy war aspect should be waged
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Islam Practices (Jihad + festivals) — OCR adds Eid-ul-Ghadeer and Ashura; keep greater>lesser Jihad framing accurate, anchor Surah 2:190

article_units.name: Judaism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: The nature of G-d, the Shekinah, the Covenants, the Mitzvot, sanctity of life and the afterlife

lessons.title: The Nature of G-d and the Divine Presence
lessons.description: G-d as One, Creator, Judge and Eternal; the problem of evil; the Shekinah and the feminine aspects of G-d.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the terms G-d as One, Creator, Law-Giver, Judge and Eternal; the significance for Jews of being All-powerful, All-good, All-knowing, Everywhere, Beyond time and space, Concerned with humanity, Intervening, Transcendent and immanent
Issues related to the nature of G-d, including the problem of evil and suffering
Common and divergent emphases including beliefs about the Last Day as Judgement day and judgements made by G-d on Rosh Hashannah
The meaning and origins of the term Shekinah as the manifest presence of G-d, and its significance in Judaism
Association of Shekinah with the feminine aspects of G-d, including the Sefirot (powers/emanations of G-d) and G-d's creative nature
Common and divergent emphases on Shekinah, including understanding the term as synonymous with G-d or as G-d descending to or dwelling on Earth; Shekinah as a feminine noun first used in the Talmud
section_markers: the problem of evil and suffering
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Beliefs (nature of G-d + Shekinah) — OCR-named Sefirot and Shekinah-as-feminine; anchor Deuteronomy 6:4-9, Exodus 40:35

lessons.title: The Covenants and the Messiah
lessons.description: The Covenant at Sinai and Moses; the Covenant with Abraham and the Promised Land; the Messiah and Messianic Age.
spec_coverage: The concept of Covenant; the significance of the Covenant at Sinai (the Ten Commandments); the role of Moses within Judaism; the nature of the promises made by G-d to the Israelites
The meaning, concept and origins of the term Messiah and the role of Elijah; the importance of the Messiah in Jewish history; the characteristics of the Messiah; the importance of the Messianic Age
Different views among religious Jews regarding the nature of the Messiah and the Messianic Age, including the Messianic Age as an era of global peace and harmony
The concept of the Promised Land: to whom it was promised and in return for what; the origins of the belief in the Covenant with Abraham
The significance of the Covenant with Abraham; the role of Abraham and his importance in Judaism; common and divergent emphases including attitudes towards the State of Israel
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Beliefs (Covenants + Messiah) — OCR groups Sinai, Abraham, Promised Land and Messiah; anchor Genesis 12:1-3, Micah 4:1-3

lessons.title: The Mitzvot and Key Moral Principles
lessons.description: The Mitzvot and their groupings; positive and negative commandments; ethical and ritual Mitzvot; Pikuach Nefesh.
spec_coverage: The meaning and significance of the term Mitzvot; different groupings: positive commandments (aseh) and negative commandments (ta'ashe)
The meaning of Divine Providence for Jews; the relationship between free will and the Mitzvot
Key moral principles, including the preservation of human life as a principle that takes precedence over all other commandments (Pikuach Nefesh)
Common and divergent emphases on the Mitzvot, including the importance of interpersonal relationships as the principle underlying some Mitzvot
The concepts of ethical and ritual Mitzvot and how they create relationship between man and G-d and/or man and man; the difference between, and significance of, ethical and ritual Mitzvot
Issues related to the Mitzvot, including the existence of different lists compiled by scholars
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Beliefs (Mitzvot) — OCR splits aseh/ta'ashe and ethical/ritual Mitzvot; anchor Deuteronomy 30:19, Book of Jonah (Divine Providence)

lessons.title: Sanctity of Life and the Afterlife
lessons.description: The sanctity of life and Pikuach Nefesh; soul and body, resurrection, judgement, Sheol, Gan Eden and Gehenna.
spec_coverage: The meaning and concept of the sanctity of life; the significance Judaism places on the sanctity of human life
The concept and meaning of Pikuach Nefesh (the obligation to save life) and its significance in Jewish personal, social and community life
Common and divergent emphases on the sanctity of life, including the difference between human and non-human lives, and whether Pikuach Nefesh extends to relieving suffering/illness
The concepts and meaning for Jews of: the distinction between soul and body, Resurrection, Judgement, Sheol, Gan Eden and Gehenna

The relationship between soul and body and its significance for Jewish attitudes towards life after death; the importance of beliefs about life after death; different ideas about the resurrection of the body
Common and divergent emphases on the concept of Judgement, including different ideas about the role of judgement in determining the nature of life after death
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Beliefs (sanctity of life + afterlife) — OCR-named Sheol/Gan Eden/Gehenna; anchor Genesis 2:7, Daniel 12:2-3

article_units.name: Judaism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: The synagogue, prayer, the Tenakh and Talmud, Shabbat, festivals, dietary laws and rituals

lessons.title: Worship, Prayer and the Law
lessons.description: The synagogue and its features; the Amidah and private prayer; the Tenakh as Written Law and the Talmud as Oral Law.
spec_coverage: The structure and importance of the synagogue: design, artefacts, services, the role of the synagogue, and worship in the home

The significance of the Ark, the Bimah, the lack of representation of G-d, the Ner Tamid and the Mikveh; the nature and importance of the Torah readings, prayers and sermons; the connection between the synagogue and the Temple
Common and divergent emphases, including separating women and men in an Orthodox synagogue

The role and importance of prayer in Jewish worship, including the Amidah (the standing prayer); the role of private prayer; the three daily periods of prayer, spontaneous prayer, recitation of the Shema and Grace after meals, teaching children to pray and the direction faced when praying
The importance of prayer for praise, confession, thanksgiving and supplication; appropriate attire for prayer

The form and content of the Tenakh (the Written Law); the Chumash and the Sefer Torah; the nature of the Talmud (the Oral Law) and its relationship to the Torah; the use of the Tenakh and Talmud in public and private worship
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Practices (synagogue + prayer) + OCR-specific Tenakh/Talmud (Written vs Oral Law); anchor Deuteronomy 6:4 (Shema)

lessons.title: Shabbat and Festivals
lessons.description: The observance of Shabbat; Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, the Pilgrim Festivals, Sukkot, Hanukkah, Pesach and Shavuot.
spec_coverage: The meaning, origins and significance of Shabbat; the traditions and Mitzvot associated with it; the preparation, lighting of candles, Shabbat meal, Havdalah and Kiddush; Shabbat services in synagogue and home; different understandings of what is prohibited
The origins and importance of Rosh Hashanah, including Teshuva, the Shofar, symbolic foods, the synagogue service and Tashlich
The origins and importance of Yom Kippur, including the connection to Rosh Hashanah, the Book of Life, Kapparah, the rules, fasting, the synagogue services and Neilah
The origins and importance of the Pilgrim Festivals, including the story of the Exodus, the importance of chametz and the Seder meal
The origins and importance of Sukkot (building of sukkah and the four species), Hanukkah, Pesach and Shavuot; issues with reconciling dates in different calendars
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Practices (Shabbat + festivals) — OCR adds Sukkot/Hanukkah/Shavuot detail; anchor Exodus 20:8-11, Leviticus 23:42-43

lessons.title: Dietary Laws and Rites of Passage
lessons.description: Kosher and Terefah dietary laws; birth ceremonies and Brit Milah; Bar/Bat Mitzvah; marriage; and burial rites.
spec_coverage: The origin and nature of dietary laws; the mitzvot regarding the slaughter and consumption of animals, poultry, fish, fruit and vegetables, and meat with milk; the meaning of Kosher and Terefah; the impact of dietary laws on Jewish lifestyle

The meaning and importance of rites of passage; Jewish birth ceremonies including the welcoming of a baby girl, the connection between Brit Milah and the covenant with Abraham, the circumcision, the roles of the father, Mohel and Sandek
The form and meaning of Bar/Bat Mitzvah including preparation, the nature of the service and Bat Chayil
The meaning and importance of Kiddushin as the betrothal ceremony; the nature and importance of the Ketubah, the Huppah, the drinking of wine, the ring, the breaking of the glass and the blessings

The meaning and importance of burial rites including the nature of burial, the tearing of clothes and the Kaddish; common and divergent emphases including attitudes towards Bat Mitzvah and the role of women
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Judaism Practices (kashrut + rites of passage) — OCR names Mohel/Sandek/Bat Chayil; anchor Leviticus 11, Genesis 17:9-12

article_units.name: Buddhism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: The Buddha, the Dhamma, the Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path, human personality and ethics

lessons.title: The Buddha and the Dhamma
lessons.description: The life of the Buddha and the Four Sights; the Dhamma; dependent origination and the Three Marks of Existence.
spec_coverage: The life of Buddha: his early life, the Four Sights, the defeat of Mara, Enlightenment and Nibbana; the importance of Buddha for Buddhists in the modern world
The meaning of the term Dhamma (eternal law and Buddha's teachings); the Dhamma as one of the Three Jewels
The meaning of dependent origination or conditionality; the relationship between dependent origination and the cycle of samsara (rebirth)
The Three Marks of Existence and their meaning: Dukkha, Impermanence (anicca/anitya), No fixed self or soul (anatta/anataman); the significance of the three marks for Buddhists
The 12 links (nidanas) and how one leads to the next over three lifetimes; common and divergent definitions of the Dhamma
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Beliefs (Buddha + Three Marks) — OCR names the 12 nidanas and the Tibetan Wheel of Life; anchor Dhammapada 35-36

lessons.title: The First and Second Noble Truths
lessons.description: The nature of life as suffering and the three types of dukkha; the cause of suffering, tanha and the three poisons.
spec_coverage: The First Noble Truth about the nature of life as suffering (dukkha); the three types of suffering: dukkha-dukkha (painful experiences), viparinama-dukkha (the changing nature of things), sankhara-dukkha (all-pervasive suffering)
The nature and significance of the different forms of suffering in Buddhist teaching; the interconnections between different forms of suffering
The Second Noble Truth about the cause of suffering and its forms; the nature of unsatisfactoriness (samudaya) and how it creates dukkha; the nature of craving (tanha) and how it creates dukkha
The form and significance of the three poisons/fires: Lobha (attachment), Dosa (aversion/aggression), Moha (ignorance); the relationship between the three poisons and suffering
Common and divergent ways of understanding ignorance (confusion or delusion), attachment (desire, greed or passion) and aversion (anger or hatred)
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Beliefs (Four Noble Truths) — OCR breaks them into separate spec areas; anchor Dhammacakkappavattana sutta

lessons.title: The Third and Fourth Noble Truths
lessons.description: The end of suffering and nibbana; Enlightenment; the Eightfold Path and the Threefold Way of sila, samadhi and panna.
spec_coverage: The Third Noble Truth about the end of suffering (dukkha); the meaning of the term nibbana (to extinguish); common and divergent ways of understanding nibbana, including as extinguishing the three poisons/fires
The different meanings given to the term Enlightenment; the cessation of craving/desire (tanha/trsna); different ways of understanding the relationship between nibbana and the cycle of rebirth
The Fourth Noble Truth about the way to eliminate suffering; the elements of the Eightfold Path (magga) and its importance and grouping for Buddhists
The elements of the Threefold Way: ethics (sila), meditation (samadhi) and wisdom (panna); the importance of the Threefold Way; the relationship between the Eightfold Path and the Threefold Way
Common and divergent ways of putting the Eightfold Path into practice in everyday life
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Beliefs (Eightfold Path) — OCR pairs Eightfold Path with the Threefold Way; anchor Magga-vibhanga Sutta

lessons.title: Human Personality, Destiny and Ethics
lessons.description: The five khandas, sunyata and buddha-nature; Arahant and Bodhisattva ideals; kamma, metta and the Five Precepts.
spec_coverage: The concept of the five aggregates (khandas) in Theravada Buddhism and their relationship to anicca, anatta and dependent origination
The Mahayana concepts of sunyata (emptiness), tathagatagarbha (the potential to become a buddha) and buddha-nature (the inherent buddhahood of all sentient beings)
The meaning and characteristics of Arahant/Arhat, Bodhisattvas and Buddhas; the paths and stages by which these states are achieved; Bodhisattva ideals, Buddhahood and Pure Land

The meaning of Kamma/Karma and rebirth/rebecoming (punabbhava), Compassion (karuna), Loving kindness (metta/maitri), the Five Precepts (pancha sila) and the Six perfections (paramitas); the role and significance of ethical principles

The concept of internalisation of virtue; skilful and unskilful action and their relationship to kamma and rebirth; the importance of the Middle Way for moral conduct; balancing compassion with wisdom
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Beliefs (human personality + ethics) + Mahayana concepts; OCR names Heart/Diamond Sutta and Amida Buddha; anchor Karaniya Metta Sutta

article_units.name: Buddhism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: Worship and meditation, sacred places, the Sangha, festivals and attitudes to death

lessons.title: Worship, Meditation and Sacred Places
lessons.description: Forms of worship including puja, chanting, mantra and malas; types of meditation; temples, viharas and shrines.
spec_coverage: The role and significance of different forms of worship: Meditation, Chanting, Puja and devotional ritual, Mantra, Malas, Offerings, and the significance of worship in the temple and the home
The purpose of devotional ritual; the relationship between devotional worship and the aim of ending dukkha; the importance and meaning of artefacts like malas
The form, focus and aim of types of meditation: Samatha, Maitri or metta bhavana, Vipassana, Zazen, Mindfulness, Visualisation; the relationship between meditation and the eightfold path
The importance, features and functions of: Temples, Gompas and viharas, Shrines, Sites of pilgrimage, Artefacts and offerings, Retreats

The events that take place in different significant places, including Bodh Gaya and the Deer Park at Sarnath; the meaning of key artefacts and the images of the Buddha and his hand positions (mudras); the importance of undertaking pilgrimages
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Practices (meditation + worship + places) — OCR names Bodh Gaya/Sarnath and mudras; anchor Dhammapada 183

lessons.title: The Sangha and Festivals
lessons.description: The Sangha and the Three Jewels; monastic and lay sangha; the Ten Precepts; Wesak, Vassa and major festivals.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the term Sangha as one of the Three Jewels; the role and importance of the monastic sangha and the lay sangha
The Ten Precepts observed by monks and nuns; the ordination of women into the monastic sangha; rules observed within monasteries

The origins, associated stories and customs of the festivals: Wesak or Hanamatsuri (Theravada/Mahayana), Vassa/Rain Retreat (Theravada), Uposatha Days (Theravada), Parinirvana day (Mahayana), Lama Tsong Khapa Day (Tibetan)
The importance of marking different parts of the Buddha's life; the purpose of Vassa and its observance by lay Buddhists; the purpose of Uposatha days
The purpose of festivals not connected to the Buddha directly, their popularity and place within Buddhism, including Lama Tsong Khapa day; the influence of local culture on festival practices
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Practices (Sangha + festivals) — OCR names Lama Tsong Khapa Day and Hanamatsuri; anchor Dhammapada 360-369

lessons.title: Attitudes to Death and Mourning
lessons.description: Death and mourning in Theravada, Tibetan and Japanese traditions; the Tibetan Book of the Dead, Bardo and Obon.
spec_coverage: Ceremonies and rituals associated with death and mourning: in Theravada communities, in Tibet (Tibetan Book of the Dead), and in Japan (Obon)
The significance of death and death customs in Buddhism; Buddhist beliefs about death and rebirth; the influence of local culture on death and mourning rituals
The importance of death rituals for the person who has died and for their family; the meaning of death rituals within the framework of Kamma, rebirth and the six realms of existence
The significance of the Tibetan Book of the Dead and the transition period between life and death (Bardo); the events and significance of Obon
Death and the Buddha's teaching about impermanence
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Buddhism Practices (death/funerals) — OCR names Bardo, Obon and the Tibetan Book of the Dead; anchor Dhammapada 37

article_units.name: Hinduism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: Atman and Brahman, samsara and karma, the nature of reality, the deities, dharma and human concerns

lessons.title: The Eternal Self, Samsara and Karma
lessons.description: Atman and Brahman; samsara, maya, detachment and moksha; karma as cosmic justice; sakam and nishkam karma.
spec_coverage: Atman as the eternal self, the part liberated from Samsara; Atman as identical with Brahman and as distinct from Brahman; common and divergent understandings of atman and liberation (moksha)

The meaning of the terms Samsara, Maya, Detachment and Moksha and their significance and interconnection; the relationship between rebirth in samsara and karma; the possibility of being jivan mukti (liberated while alive)
The meaning of the term karma and its role in Hindu life and rebirth; karma as causality and a form of cosmic justice; karma as the connection between action and consequence

The state of jivan mukti and its relationship to karma; the effect of positive and negative karma within samsara (parabdha karma); the creation of karma through choices in the current lifetime (kriyamana karma)
Sakam karma (with results in mind) and nishkam karma (desireless) and the way these relate to rebirth and liberation
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Beliefs (atman + samsara + karma) — OCR names parabdha/kriyamana/sakam/nishkam karma; anchor Bhagavad Gita II 22

lessons.title: The Nature of Reality and Cosmology
lessons.description: Maya, Loka, Devas and Asuras; the realms of the Tri-Murti; prakriti, purusha, the trigunas and the Mahayuga.
spec_coverage: The meanings of the terms Maya, Loka, Devas and Asuras; the concept of Loka (world/realm/space) and the ways the Lokas are divided

The heavenly realms of the Tri-Murti: Brahma-Loka, Shiva-Loka and Vishnu-Loka/Vaikuntha; the inhabitants of the different realms and the belief that people are born into different realms as a result of karma
The nature of the material world; the meaning of prakriti, purusha and the trigunas, and their role in the creation and constitution of the material world
The cycle of creation and destruction as it applies to the universe, including the roles of the Trimurti and the Mahayuga
Common and divergent understandings of cosmology and creation, including the cyclical universe, trimurti, aum and mahayuga, and the relationship between the material world and the concept of Maya
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Beliefs (cosmology, often light) — OCR develops prakriti/purusha/trigunas and Mahayuga; anchor Nasadiya Sukta (Rig Veda)

lessons.title: The Divine: Brahman, the Deities and the Avatars
lessons.description: Saguna and Nirguna Brahman; antaryami; the Trimurti, Tridevi and Shakti; avatara and murti as the focus of worship.
spec_coverage: Different ways of understanding Brahman, with attributes (Saguna Brahman) and without attributes (Nirguna Brahman); Hindu deities as manifestations of Saguna Brahman
The role and importance of the Trimurti and the Tridevi, including the concept of Shakti and the relationship between male and female deities
The role and importance of Avatara as the incarnation or manifestation of deities in a particular physical form; the significance of Avatara in different Hindu traditions
The role and importance of Murti as the focus of worship and as an expression of an actual presence

The concept of Brahman as eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading, unlimited, infinite and impersonal (nirguna) and as the personal deity manifested in forms (saguna); the nature of Brahman as all-pervading and within the heart (antaryami); Brahman as the supreme person (Bhagavan or Ishvara)
section_markers: Jesus and the Buddha as avatars
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Beliefs (Brahman + deities + avatars) — OCR-named antaryami and Tridevi; anchor Kena Upanishad I, avatars of Vishnu

lessons.title: The Four Aims of Life, Dharma and Human Concerns
lessons.description: The Purusharthas; sanatana dharma and varna; free will, suffering and the Hindu virtues (yamas) including ahimsa.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the term Dharma (dependent on context) and its role and significance in Hindu life; the relationship between dharma and varna, ashrama, artha, karma and moksha
Sanatana dharma (the eternal dharma) as a name some Hindus give to their religion, including ancient and universal truths; the relationship between an individual's dharma and the concept of karma
Common and divergent emphases on the four aims of human life (Purusharthas), including different ways of understanding varna and its function in society
Hindu understanding of the concepts of free will, suffering and virtue, and their relationship to karma and samsara

The meaning and importance of Hindu virtues/moral duties (yamas), including harmlessness/non-violence (Ahimsa), compassion (daya), self-control/restraint (dama) and giving (dana); the relationship between virtues and particular elements of dharma
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Beliefs (four aims + dharma) — OCR groups Purusharthas with yamas/virtues; anchor Bhagavad Gita XVI 1-3

article_units.name: Hinduism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: The four margas, forms of worship, sacred places and pilgrimage, festivals and ethical concerns

lessons.title: Ways of Living: The Four Margas
lessons.description: The four margas (jnana, bhakti, karma and raja yoga); varnashramadharma; svadharma, sewa and dana.
spec_coverage: The meaning of the four margas: Jnana yoga, Bhakti yoga, Karma yoga and Astanga or raja yoga; different Hindu understandings of living a good life and seeking liberation
The approach and practices associated with the different margas; the significance of Varnashramadharma for individuals and society
The relationship between these ways of living and the concepts of karma and moksha
The role and importance of Hindu approaches to social concerns: Svadharma (personal duty), Sewa (service) and Dana (giving)
The common and divergent emphases put on these ways of living, including the possibility of following more than one yoga
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Practices (yogas/margas) — OCR names all four margas with their Gita anchors and svadharma/sewa/dana

lessons.title: Worship, Sacred Places and Pilgrimage
lessons.description: Havan, puja, japa, bhajan, kirtan and darshan; sacred places; holy people; pilgrimage to Varanasi and the Ganges.
spec_coverage: Different Hindu understandings of the role, forms and importance of worship: Havan or homa, Puja, Meditation, Japa, Bhajan or kirtan, and Darshan
The nature and importance of sacred places and spaces for Hindu worship: Temples, Shrines, Sites of pilgrimage, Outdoors, Hills and rivers
The role and importance of holy people, including gurus and sadhus/sadhvis; the role and importance of sacred plants and animals
The purpose and practice of pilgrimage; sites of pilgrimage including Varanasi and the river Ganges, and the purpose of pilgrimage to different sites
The importance of darshan and the different forms it can take in relation to murti, holy people and sites of holy places
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Practices (puja + pilgrimage) — OCR names Varanasi/Ganges and darshan forms; anchor Gayatri Mantra

lessons.title: Festivals and Ethical Concerns
lessons.description: Holi, Navaratri, Diwali, Ganesh Chaturthi and Raksha Bandhan; Hindu attitudes to the environment and social issues.
spec_coverage: Hindu festivals, their origins, associated deities, stories and customs: Holi, Navaratri, Diwali, Maha Shivatrari, Ganesh Chaturthi and Raksha Bandhan; different Hindu attitudes to their meaning and importance; why Ganesh Chaturthi is so widely celebrated
Hindu attitudes to, and beliefs and teachings about, the environment and the natural world, including the treatment of animals and the environment
Hinduism and social issues: social responsibility, social inclusion and women's rights

The ways Hindu attitudes are put into practice through charitable projects, including the Assisi Declarations on nature (1986), the protection of sacred cows through goshallas and the Ahimsa Foundation for Cattle Protection, and Sewa International (Sewa UK)
The relationship of these to karma, the cycle of samsara and the yamas, especially daya (compassion), dama (restraint) and kshama (patience/tolerance)
section_markers: the work and example of Gandhi
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel Hinduism Practices (festivals) + OCR-specific ethics (Assisi Declarations, goshallas, Sewa International); anchor Gandhi's example

article_units.name: Relationships and Families
article_units.subtitle: Marriage, family, sexuality, divorce and the equality of men and women across religious traditions

lessons.title: Marriage, the Family and Sexuality
lessons.description: Religious attitudes to family and marriage; the marriage ceremony; same-sex marriage, cohabitation and celibacy.
spec_coverage: Religious attitudes towards the role and purpose of the family
Religious attitudes towards the importance and purposes of marriage; the significance of beliefs and teachings reflected in a religious marriage ceremony; reasons for differences in practice
Same-sex marriage and consideration of beliefs, teachings and attitudes relating to civil partnership, pre-marital sex, cohabitation, celibacy and contraception
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: fidelity, understandings of sexuality, ethical modes of relationship
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups (Christianity primary; Islam as a second-religion lens)
section_markers: Muslim attitudes towards the family and marriage
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS Relationships theme — OCR is multi-faith through one chosen religion; draw primarily on Christianity (anchor Matthew 19:4-6), use Islam as second lens

lessons.title: Divorce and the Roles of Men and Women
lessons.description: The ethics of divorce, annulment and remarriage; the roles of men and women in family, community and upbringing.
spec_coverage: Beliefs, teachings and attitudes relating to the ethics of divorce, annulment and remarriage
Consideration of beliefs, teachings and attitudes relating to the roles of men and women in family relationships, religious communities and the religious upbringing of children
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: equality of men and women, freedom of choice and restrictions on it, duty to family and community
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS Relationships theme (divorce + gender roles) — OCR anchors Matthew 5:31-32, Ephesians 5; multi-faith framing

lessons.title: Equality and Gender in Society
lessons.description: Religious teachings about equality; the influence of culture; prejudice and discrimination on grounds of gender.
spec_coverage: Religious teachings and beliefs about equality; the influence of culture on attitudes and views about equality
Religious views on the importance of equality for individuals, communities and society
Religious attitudes and beliefs about prejudice and discrimination on the basis of gender; teachings about equality and discrimination in relation to gender
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: the relationship between religion and culture, justification of equality, equality and difference, gender inequalities, embedded inequalities
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups
section_markers: Archbishop Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission in South Africa
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS equality material — OCR-named Archbishop Tutu/TRC; anchor Galatians 3:28, Genesis 1:27; multi-faith framing

article_units.name: The Existence of God and Ultimate Reality
article_units.subtitle: Arguments for God, the problem of evil, the nature of reality and religious experience

lessons.title: The Question of God and the Problem of Evil
lessons.description: Religious understandings of what God is like and God's relationship with the world; God as good; human suffering.
spec_coverage: Religious understandings of the concept of God: different teachings about what God is like, about God's relationship with the world, and about God's relationship with humanity; reasons for different views
Religious beliefs and views on God as good; understandings of the meaning of goodness in the context of God's actions
Religious beliefs, teachings and views on the relationship between God and human suffering
Key philosophical concepts: the nature of the Christian (or chosen religion's) God, the problem of the existence of evil and a world designed by a God who is good
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS existence-of-God theme — OCR multi-faith via chosen religion; anchor 1 John 4:8, Luke 15:11-32; Islam as second lens

lessons.title: Arguments for the Existence of God
lessons.description: The cosmological, first cause, teleological and moral arguments; the anthropic principle; soul-making.
spec_coverage: Philosophical views on the nature of reality and the reasons for belief in God: the world as designed (the argument from design and purpose), the world as requiring a cause (the first cause argument), the world as formed for humanity (the Anthropic principle in Genesis), and the world and moral consequence, soul-making and judgement
The value and importance of arguments for the existence of God
Key philosophical concepts: arguments about the existence of God, ideas about the purpose of the world, ethical living
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS philosophy theme (design + first cause + moral arguments) — OCR names the Anthropic principle and soul-making; anchor Psalm 14:1

lessons.title: Experiencing God: Revelation and Miracles
lessons.description: How believers think God is revealed; forms of religious experience: conversion, mystical, charismatic and visions.
spec_coverage: Different ways in which believers think God might be revealed: meeting inspirational people, through scripture/the Word of God, Jesus Christ (or the chosen religion's founder/messengers), figures from religious history, God acting in the world, conscience and miracles
Different forms of religious experience: conversion, mystical, charismatic and ecstatic, visions, worship and the sacraments
Key philosophical concepts: revelation by the divine, miracles, perception of the divine
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS revelation/religious-experience material — OCR names conversion/mystical/charismatic; anchor Acts 9:1-6, John 1:14

article_units.name: Religion, Peace and Conflict
article_units.subtitle: Violence, war and Just War, pacifism and peacemaking, forgiveness, reconciliation and justice

lessons.title: Violence, War and Just War Theory
lessons.description: Religious teachings about violence; terrorism and its causes; Just War Theory, Holy War and modern warfare.
spec_coverage: The way religious teachings about violence are applied and understood by individuals and religious communities, and their role in society

The role of individuals, communities and society in violent conflicts; the causes of terrorism; the relationship between religion, politics and terrorism in the 21st century; different attitudes towards terrorism and its causes
Justifications for waging war: Just War Theory; the concept of Holy War; religious attitudes to behaviours during war
Different attitudes to conventional warfare (armies in conflict), technological warfare (drones and surgical strikes) and apocalyptic warfare (nuclear)
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: forms of violence, war, justification of violence, Just War theory
section_markers: Thomas Aquinas and the conditions for war to be just
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS peace-and-conflict theme (Just War + Holy War) — OCR adds drone/apocalyptic warfare; anchor Aquinas/Just War, Micah 4:3

lessons.title: Peace and Peacemaking
lessons.description: Absolute and conditional pacifism; non-violence; how individuals and communities work for peace and justice.
spec_coverage: The concept of pacifism, including absolute pacifism and conditional pacifism; different religious teachings, beliefs and attitudes in relation to pacifism
Different ways individuals, communities and society work for peace: how religious teachings about peace are applied and understood

Different attitudes to the use of violence to achieve peace; working for peace and justice in situations, communities and society; whether working for peace should be the most important activity for believers; non-violent action
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: pacifism, non-violence as force, value of peace
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS pacifism material — OCR names Quaker declaration 1660, MLK, Gandhi, CCND; anchor Sermon on the Mount Matthew 5:38-42

lessons.title: Forgiveness, Reconciliation and Justice
lessons.description: Forgiveness and reconciliation; teachings about justice; whether forgiveness is desirable; social justice.
spec_coverage: The concepts of forgiveness and reconciliation; different teachings and beliefs about justice, forgiveness and reconciliation, and their impact on individuals, communities and society
Whether forgiveness is either possible or desirable; different attitudes towards justice, forgiveness and reconciliation

The concepts of justice and injustice, including the relationship between peace and a just society, social justice and injustice, ways in which believers work for social justice and view social injustice
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: forgiveness, justice, fairness and injustice, reconciliation
section_markers: the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of South Africa
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS forgiveness/justice material — OCR-named TRC South Africa; anchor Matthew 6:12-14, Matthew 18:35; multi-faith framing

article_units.name: Dialogue Between Religious and Non-Religious Beliefs
article_units.subtitle: Secularism, religion in public life, inter-faith dialogue and engagement with humanism and atheism

lessons.title: Challenges for Religion in a Secular Society
lessons.description: Religion as Britain's established faith; secularisation and humanism; clashes with secular law and medical ethics.
spec_coverage: The importance of religious traditions in British society; the established religion in a country of diverse religious traditions; the Monarch as Supreme Governor of the Church of England; the role of religion in public life (bishops in the House of Lords, services to mark key events, public holidays, church schools)
The concept of secularisation: the place of religion in a secular society, the effects of secularisation on religion, the rise of humanism
Potential clashes between religious and secular values in education: secular ethics and values in school, faith schools

Potential clashes between religion, tradition and secular law: religious teachings about marriage, responses to forced/arranged/child marriages, attitudes to equality and potential clashes with equality laws
Potential clashes between religious teachings and scientific development in medical ethics: euthanasia and the right to die, abortion, genetic manipulation and the creation of life
Key concepts: secularism, tolerance, freedom of belief/expression/practice, equality in society, the value of human life, self-determination
section_markers: Supreme Governor of the Church of England
bishops in the House of Lords
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS dialogue/secularism material — OCR is England-specific (Supreme Governor, bishops in Lords, Education Act 1988); anchor Exodus 20:13

lessons.title: Dialogue Within and Between Religious Groups
lessons.description: Exclusivism, inclusivism, pluralism, ecumenism and inter-faith dialogue; national identity and proselytisation.
spec_coverage: Different teachings, beliefs and attitudes of believers towards each other and towards other religious groups, including exclusivism, inclusivism, pluralism, ecumenism, intra-faith communication and inter-faith dialogue
The importance of inter-faith dialogue in 21st century Britain
The relationship between religion and wider society, including religion and national identity and proselytisation
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: consensus, diversity, uniformity, freedom of choice, freedom of expression
Awareness of the justifications believers give for different views, from the perspectives of different denominations and groups
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS inter-faith material — OCR names exclusivism/inclusivism/pluralism; anchor John 14:6, Matthew 28:18-20; multi-faith framing

lessons.title: Dialogue with Non-Religious Worldviews
lessons.description: Religious attitudes to atheism, agnosticism, humanism and secularism; shared values and areas of disagreement.
spec_coverage: Different views and attitudes towards non-religious worldviews; values and ideals shared with atheism, agnosticism, humanism and secularism
The significance of shared values and ideals between religious and non-religious groups for individuals, communities and society
Whether secular values should take precedence over religious values
Potential areas of disagreement and difference between religion and atheism, agnosticism, humanism and secularism, and their significance for individuals, communities and society
Key philosophical and ethical concepts: beliefs, religious values, secular values
lessons.transfer: AQA/Edexcel RS humanism/atheism material — OCR-named BHA, National Secular Society, Tony Blair Foundation; anchor Matthew 22:37-40
